newsitem.title: USA: NY physical coffee - sluggish tone persists.
newsitem.headline: NY physical coffee - sluggish tone persists.

text.p: The New York physical market remained quiet this week, with few prompt sales, as roasters continued to stick to the sidelines, traders said.
Although a downturn in CSCE futures prices this week may have inspired some price-fixing, traders said roasters' near-term needs were generally well met.
"Roasters are basically covered as far as physical purchases are concerned through June," one trader said. "All they have to do is fix."
Although supplies of quality mild coffees remained sparse, traders said concerns had eased as origins picked up the pace of shipments to take advantage of higher futures prices.

"There's quite a bit more coffee arriving and available," one dealer said. "Exporters at source are trying to solicit bids and we don't care. We have a two-to-three-week window where we can tell them to take a hike."

Traders said easing differentials on spot Colombian beans failed to tempt buyers, who still viewed the beans as unattractively expensive. May's hefty premium to second-month July also discouraged spot business, they said.
